title: CNN, MS NOW say journalists denied access to White House grounds after Trump's ban
summary: Two major news networks' journalists said they were denied access to the White House on Saturday morning, with reporters from CNN and MS NOW both going live to report about the circumstances of the…

image.caption: The CNN booth at the White House is shown after U.S. President Donald Trump announced he would ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico, in Washington, D.C., on Friday. (Evan Vucci/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Two major news networks' journalists said they were denied access to the White House on Saturday morning, with reporters from CNN and MS NOW both going live to report about the circumstances of the ban imposed by U.S. President Donald Trump.
Politico also included in White House restrictions announced by U.S. president Friday

The actions escalated Trump's long-running efforts to restrict news coverage by journalists he finds objectionable and is the latest test of First Amendment protections in the United States. Trump said on Friday he would ban both organizations and Politico because of their coverage.

CNN issued a statement saying it stood behind its reporters. "We will not be deflected from our duty to hold the government and other public bodies to account," it said. The statement was shown on the air before senior White House reporter Betsy Klein began to report on her ban.

items: Trump announces White House ban on CNN, other media outlets

blocks.text: MS NOW, which until last November was called MSNBC, also said it stands behind its journalists.

"The White House belongs to the American people and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars," the network said in a statement on Saturday. "MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy."
Trump bans CNN and other media outlets from White House
Trump said on Friday that he was barring the news channel, along with CNN and Politico, from the White House due to what he called unfavourable coverage and "fake news."
Politico journalists are typically not at the White House on Saturdays.
MS NOW White House correspondent Akayla Gardner was turned away and her entry badge was confiscated, she said on air Saturday morning.

Gardner said she had walked through two gates successfully, but once she got to where her badge needed to be scanned, an officer told her it was disabled and asked her to hand it over. He said the decision "was above him," she reported.
An MS NOW producer was able to get in, but a photographer's badge was also disabled, Gardner said.
Trump calls news outlets 'fake news'

The president wrote on his social media site on Friday that effective immediately, "I am banning" CNN, MS NOW and Politico "from the White House as a result of their constant ‘reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Minutes later, speaking at an event in the Oval Office, Trump was asked to explain his statement.

"Because they're fake news," he said. "You get so tired of reading and seeing fake news. When you look at CNN, it's just fake. That's why their ratings are no good. When you look at MS NOW ... it's fake news.

"And when you look at Politico ... the stories they wrote are fake. So there's a lot of news and there may be others to join them, and maybe they can get better," he said. "But our country has to have honest news."

blocks.text: In his second term, Trump and his administration have upped the ante and punished certain media outlets, both in the courtroom and through regulatory action. Trump has also lashed out at individual reporters in person or over social media, sometimes in strikingly personal terms.

The move follows the president's decision last year to bar Associated Press reporters from the Oval Office, Air Force One and other events in retaliation for the news outlet's decision not to follow his lead in changing the name of the Gulf of Mexico, which lies partially in Mexican and other waters.
The AP said that it would note when appropriate that Trump had ordered it renamed the "Gulf of America."
